claims.claim_text: The indexed Bruce Rogers is best supported as the Oregon graduate and Japan specialist later documented in OSS Morale Operations.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Independent institutional, contemporary, and scholarly sources connect Bruce Rogers to Oregon, prewar Japan, Japanese-language expertise, U.S. consular work, and OSS recruitment activity.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from a distinctive multi-source trajectory; the common name alone would be insufficient.
claims.temporal_assessment: The record sequence runs from a 1939 Oregon yearbook through prewar Osaka service and wartime OSS Morale Operations; exact appointment dates remain incomplete.
claims.match_notes: The identity is triangulated; unrelated typographer, Australian, and modern namesakes were rejected.

claims.claim_text: Bruce Rogers studied business administration at the University of Oregon and represented Oregon at a Japan-American Student Conference.
claims.evidence_excerpt: BRUCE ROGERS, Newberg, Business Administration ... Oregon Delegate to Japan-American Student Conference
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The university yearbook lists Rogers's field, hometown, transfer status, conference delegation, and campus organizations.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence through the later Japan-language, consular, and OSS trajectory; not based on the common name alone.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly documented in the 1939 University of Oregon yearbook, before wartime OSS service.
claims.match_notes: University attendance is modeled as student status, not employment.

claims.claim_text: Before his documented OSS work, Bruce Rogers served at the U.S. consulate in Osaka, although his title and dates remain unknown.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Bruce Rogers, once of the U.S. consulate in Osaka
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Charlotte DeForest recalled recognizing Rogers from Japan and identified his earlier U.S. consular affiliation before describing his wartime government research.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity bridge from Oregon-to-Japan activity, Japanese-language expertise, and independently documented OSS Morale Operations work.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented as an earlier Japan affiliation, but not established as the immediate predecessor to OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The qualified claim preserves the missing title and dates and does not label the consulate an immediate OSS predecessor.
